title: Console UI: batching SLO tier selection + recommended tier + “why this profile” explanations
creator: Alicia Perez
body:
## Context
Runtime is shipping workload-aware batching defaults mapped to 3 customer-facing latency SLO tiers: **fast / standard / cost-efficient**. Console needs:
1) A place to select a tier (where allowed)
2) A **recommended tier** hint (Optimize + runtime heuristics) without over-promising
3) A “**why this profile**” drill-down that explains the effective tier/profile and what influenced the selection

This ticket covers UX + copy + interaction design. Implementation will be tracked in ENG tickets; this ticket should output a clear spec and acceptance criteria for engineering.

## Goals
- Make tier selection discoverable and safe (minimize foot-guns)
- Clarify **effective behavior** when multiple layers apply (customer override > route policy > tier default)
- Provide lightweight but useful explanations (“why”) that map to runtime reason codes (ENG-18426)
- Support Hosted + Dedicated flows; Private should be consistent but may be less polished in v1

## Non-goals
- Building a full auto-tuner UI (out of scope per project)
- Exposing every scheduler knob in Console (advanced overrides remain for Dedicated / support-guided flows)

## Proposed information architecture (IA)
### A) Route-level policy (primary surface)
Location: **Console → API Routes → {route} → Performance** (existing place for model selection / rate limits)
Add a section: **Batching & latency tier**
- Tier dropdown: Fast / Standard / Cost-efficient
- Helper text: “Controls batching aggressiveness and latency targets. Defaults are workload-aware; you can override per route.”
- Link: “Learn about tiers” → public docs page (tracked in ENG-18432)

Why route-level?
- Matches customer mental model: “this endpoint should be fast”
- Avoids request-level churn and accidental per-request divergence
- Works for both Hosted and Dedicated in a consistent way

### B) Request-level override (secondary, not the main UI)
We should not encourage request-level tier selection in Console UI (SDK headers/params exist), but we should:
- Display that request-level overrides are possible in docs/examples
- In Console, show a read-only hint: “Requests may override this tier via SDK параметer/header” (copy TBD) to reduce confusion when customers see mixed telemetry.

### C) Dedicated tenant / cluster override (admin-only)
Location: **Console → Dedicated → {cluster/tenant} → Overrides**
- Shows effective precedence
- Allows admin-only default tier for a tenant/cluster, with warning that route policies may override unless locked
- Copy should match precedence rules from ENG-18430

## Recommended tier experience
We need to show a recommendation without implying a guarantee.

### Where to show it
- In the same **Batching & latency tier** section, show:
  - “Recommended: Standard” (badge)
  - “Based on your traffic shape in the last 7 days” or “Based on typical workloads for this model” when traffic is insufficient

### Recommendation states
1) **Confident (observed traffic)**
- Copy: “Recommended: Standard (based on p95 latency + prompt length distribution over last 7 days)” 
- CTA: “View details” (opens side panel with the factors)

2) **Low confidence (insufficient traffic)**
- Copy: “Recommended: Standard (limited recent traffic; using model defaults)” 

3) **No recommendation (missing telemetry / new route)**
- Copy: “No recommendation yet”
- CTA: “Run a test” (links to benchmarking guide / in-console ‘Generate sample load’ is out of scope)

### Guardrails and warnings
- If user selects **Fast** and the route is primarily long prompts + non-streaming, show warning: “Fast tier may reduce batching efficiency and increase cost. Consider Standard unless you have strict tail latency requirements.”
- If user selects **Cost-efficient** for a streaming endpoint, show warning: “Cost-efficient tier may increase time-to-first-token under bursty load.”

(These warnings are UX-only; runtime guards happen elsewhere.)

## “Why this profile” drill-down
Customers need to understand:
- What tier is configured
- What tier is effectively applied at runtime
- Why the runtime chose a specific profile (or why it fell back)

### Entry points
1) Route page: “Why this profile?” link under tier selector
2) Observability dashboard panels: clicking a tier badge opens the same side panel filtered to that route/model

### Side panel content (v1)
**Header:** Effective batching profile
- Effective tier: e.g., “Standard”
- Effective profile name/version: e.g., “standard@r1.22 / llama3-family / H100” (exact naming TBD)
- Last updated timestamp (config change)

**Section 1: What influenced this** (top 3–5 bullets)
Sources should map to reason codes (ENG-18426). Examples:
- “Tier set by route policy (you)”
- “Workload signal: streaming=true”
- “Workload signal: prompt length mostly 1–2k tokens”
- “Model constraint: max batch tokens capped for this quantization variant”
- “Overload mode active 2% of requests (admission control)”

**Section 2: Precedence** (explain effective tier)
A compact precedence visualization:
- Customer override (Dedicated) → Route policy → Tier default
- Highlight which one is active; show inactive layers as dimmed

**Section 3: What this means** (customer-facing outcomes)
- “Fast: tighter wait budget; lower batching; best for strict p99; higher cost”
- “Standard: balanced defaults”
- “Cost-efficient: more aggressive batching; may increase tail latency under bursts”

**Section 4: Related metrics (deep link)**
Buttons linking to pre-filtered dashboards:
- Latency by tier (p50/p95/p99)
- Batch size distribution
- Queue depth / admission control rate

## Copy / naming decisions (open items)
- Use **fast / standard / cost-efficient** (confirmed in PM thread; see Nikhil + Aditya email 2026-02-03). Avoid “realtime” due to overpromise.
- Use “tier” consistently (not “mode”) to match docs and SDK.
- “Why this profile?” vs “Why this tier?”
  - Recommendation: “Why this profile?” because runtime may select a constrained profile within a tier due to model/hardware constraints.

## Edge cases to handle
- Route pinned to a model that doesn’t support a tier’s preferred profile: UI should show “Profile adjusted due to model constraints” (reason code surfaced).
- Dedicated override set but route policy differs: UI should show both and the precedence.
- Mixed outcomes across regions/hardware classes: show the effective profile name includes hardware class; side panel should include a region selector only if we have time (otherwise show “varies by region” + deep link).
- Kill switch / rollout gating: if tiered defaults disabled, UI should show read-only state: “Tier selection not available (feature not enabled for your org)” and link to support.

## Deliverables
- Figma: route page updates + side panel + dedicated override page updates
- Copy deck for docs/console strings (handoff to DevEx)
- Interaction notes + acceptance criteria for ENG

## Acceptance criteria (for design sign-off)
- Tier selector is present in Route → Performance for eligible orgs and respects permissions
- Recommendation badge is visible and includes confidence messaging
- “Why this profile?” panel clearly explains effective tier, precedence, and at least 3 reason-code bullets
- Warnings appear for streaming + cost-efficient and long prompts + fast (copy can be refined)
- Dedicated override page communicates precedence with route policies

## Links
- Confluence design spec (placeholder): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-ui-batching-recommendations.json
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-batching-profiles-slo-tiers.json
- Reason codes ticket: ENG-18426
- Config precedence ticket: ENG-18430

## Notes
- We should keep v1 explainability intentionally “human readable” and avoid exposing raw scheduler knobs.
- Avoid phrasing that implies fixed latency guarantees; tie claims to SLO tiers and observed metrics.
comments: 2026-01-16 (Alicia Perez): Created. Need a design pass that makes tier selection feel like a simple policy choice, not an infra knob. Please align language with PM messaging draft and avoid ‘realtime’.

2026-01-23 (Kenji Nakamura): Initial IA proposal: Route-level is primary. Dedicated overrides need a separate admin surface. Drafting side panel for “why” driven by reason codes; waiting on final shape from ENG-18426.

2026-02-03 (Henry Cho): Please ensure UI clarifies default behavior when user does nothing. For Hosted, most routes will implicitly be Standard unless recommendations shift; we need copy that avoids confusion with per-request overrides.

2026-02-07 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated customers will ask ‘why didn’t my override apply’. Precedence visualization is required. Also need an org/tenant permission boundary (who can change global default tier).
2026-02-13 (Allison Grant): For “why” content, please don’t require high-cardinality fields. Reason code bullets should be a small set and link to dashboards for deeper metrics.

2026-02-20 (Kenji Nakamura): Added warnings for streaming+cost-efficient and long prompts+fast. Still open: how to present region/hardware differences without adding complex UI. Suggest: show effective profile name includes hardware class and link to dashboards filtered by region.

2026-02-27 (Alicia Perez): Please proceed to Figma finalization with the side panel approach. Ensure copy doesn’t overpromise latency guarantees and uses ‘targets’ language. After Figma, we’ll sync with Chloe Martin for feasibility of panel data sources.
